name: Tabeel
overview: Tabeel is a male figure mentioned in the Bible whose enemies sought to place his son as king over Judah. There is no record of his tribal affiliation or additional personal details. His significance is primarily connected to this political ambition against Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Tabeel means 'G-d [El] is good,' reflecting a theistic affirmation common in Hebrew names. This proper name is noted in Isaiah 7:6, though it was not given by God directly.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Tabeel beyond the mention of his son, whom his enemies wanted to set over Judah as king. No other familial ties are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Tabeel's importance in the biblical narrative lies in the political intrigue surrounding his son, who was the focus of opposition forces aiming to challenge the reigning authority in Judah. This highlights the tensions and struggles for power during that period. Although little else is revealed about Tabeel himself, the mention of his son’s potential kingship indicates a notable moment of conflict in Judah’s history.
